A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DyBBT framework. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original DyBBT benchmark results, ablations, scaling experiments, training analyses, and expert evaluations, including in Appendices C and D.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds live-user experiments, confidence-trigger error analysis, cost measurements, and a quantitative failure audit.

M1.justification: The cognitive-state representation, dual-trigger switching rule, three-path S2 reasoning, SFT/PPO stages, and distillation algorithm are retained. Appendix B.5.2 newly details confidence-training augmentation and losses, but does not establish a revision to the previously described procedure.

E1.justification: MS Dialog and MultiWOZ 2.1 coverage remains. New Appendix D adds live multi-domain interactions with 30 volunteers, including intent shifts, vague expressions, and atypical repeated questions. This extends evaluation beyond simulated interactions and v1's expert judgments of fixed dialog states.

E2.justification: Existing benchmark and expert-rating comparator sets are retained. V2 adds a live-user comparison with PPO, EIERL, and random switching (Table 5), and evaluates LLM_DP in the new cost comparison (Table 9). Comparator participation expands in these evaluations, without introducing a new baseline algorithm.

E3.justification: New protocols cover 30 volunteers completing 300 dialog goals with a 40-turn limit and satisfaction ratings, analysis of 200 confidence interventions, and a 1,000-dialog audit checked by three experts. Appendix E.7 adds absolute latency and token-based API-cost measurement. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, and ablation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a confidence-condition error taxonomy and four intervention cases (E.3), three live-user cases (D.2), a deployment-cost analysis (E.7), and quantified failure modes (E.9). The original component ablations, sensitivity analyses, scaling studies, and simulated cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify the same five random seeds and retain identical standard-deviation reporting for model scaling. New live-user rows use the existing plus/minus reporting style, without specifying a new uncertainty estimator, confidence interval, significance test, or increased run count.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, ablation, expert-rating, scaling, and Qwen3-mode table values are unchanged. New results include 84.7% live-user success for DyBBT-8B (Table 5), inference times of 12.5/28.7/42.1 seconds for the three cost configurations (Table 9), confidence-error proportions (Table 7), and a reported 5.2% failure-mode total (Table 11). These are added findings, not improvements over v1 under identical conditions.

T1.justification: Section 3.1.1 adds an explicit two-arm contextual-bandit formulation, an immediate-reward regret definition, and treatment of S2 as an oracle arm. Appendix A.1 changes dim(C) <= 3 to dim(C) = 3. The existing approximate-MDP assumptions, value-based regret bound, derivation sketch, and heuristic qualifications otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a structured cognitive state, bandit-inspired switching between fast and deliberative systems, and claims of strong performance, efficiency, generalization, and human alignment. Additional experiments support these retained claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of specific errors prevented by confidence triggering, emotional and atypical-user limitations, and the costs of using GPT-4 as S2. Previously qualitative failure concerns are now interpreted as infrequent and manageable for commercial tasks, with additional safeguards advised for safety-critical settings (E.9).

D1.justification: Appendix B.5.2 newly documents the 10,000-sample augmentation recipe, perturbation probabilities, confidence targets, and weighted action/confidence losses. V2 also specifies Python 3.10 and latency/API-cost accounting. The code-access link changes from a named GitHub repository to an anonymous repository; accessibility was not externally checked.

R1.justification: V2 adds focused references on metric-space bandits, continuous-state RL, Bayesian uncertainty, and LLM confidence. It replaces the original MultiWOZ citation with the MultiWOZ 2.1 paper and removes some earlier references. The overall positioning against static exploration, evolutionary methods, and heuristic dual-system switching is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, and methodology narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. Related-work subsections and analysis sections are merged, appendices are reorganized, and separate Limitations and Ethics sections appear near the conclusion. The author list also adds Yujie Liu.

P2.justification: The entire paper changes from single-column to two-column layout. The ablation table moves into the main text, four new tables present added evaluations, and retained figures and tables are resized and reflowed. Several v2 appendix listings visibly expose LaTeX caption and formatting options, introducing presentation defects.

improvement.justification: The live-user study, measured cost trade-offs, failure analyses, and confidence-training recipe improve practical assessment and reproducibility beyond v1. The gain is limited by unclear system assignment and uncertainty aggregation in the new user study, an Ethics Statement that contradicts human-participation and compensation descriptions, and malformed appendix listings. The expanded theoretical framing also retains the earlier heuristic derivation. Overall, the additional evidence and implementation detail provide a modest net improvement.
